react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged unequivocally on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top hit (FDR 8.59e-19, 7 metabolites hit), with WP:WP465 'Tryptophan metabolism' at rank 1 (FDR 4.02e-15, 6 metabolites hit). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 (p = 5.41e-09, 6 metabolites hit). The m/z-direct mummichog empirical-compound network also ranked 'Tryptophan metabolism' first (p = 0.00134, overlap size 16/17 compounds), demonstrating cross-paradigm consensus from ORA and network-activity perspectives. The KEGG hsa00380 pathway covers the full tryptophan degradation tree: the direct decarboxylation branch (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, serotonin, melatonin) and the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid → NAD+ biosynthesis). The driver metabolites span both branches, with L-tryptophan acting as the entry substrate. The convergent signal across three independent tools — two ORA implementations and one m/z network-activity method — provides high confidence that tryptophan catabolism is systemically altered in the treatment group. The presence of 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 (an aflatoxin B1 bioactivation product) suggests exposure to a xenobiotic that is known to induce IDO1-mediated tryptophan degradation along the kynurenine route, redirecting tryptophan flux away from serotonin/melatonin synthesis toward NAD+ precursor production. N-Formyl-L-glutamic acid and deoxyribose 1-phosphate appear as secondary hits in folate metabolism and the pentose phosphate pathway, respectively.

RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top hit (FDR 8.59e-19, 7 metabolites hit), with WP:WP465 'Tryptophan metabolism' at rank 1 (FDR 4.02e-15, 6 metabolites hit). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 (p = 5.41e-09, 6 metabolites hit). The m/z-direct mummichog empirical-compound network also ranked 'Tryptophan metabolism' first (p = 0.00134, overlap size 16/17 compounds), demonstrating cross-paradigm consensus from ORA and network-activity perspectives. The KEGG hsa00380 pathway covers the full tryptophan degradation tree: the direct decarboxylation branch (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, serotonin, melatonin) and the kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid → NAD+ biosynthesis). The driver metabolites span both branches, with L-tryptophan acting as the entry substrate. The convergent signal across three independent tools — two ORA implementations and one m/z network-activity method — provides high confidence that tryptophan catabolism is systemically altered in the treatment group. The presence of 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 (an aflatoxin B1 bioactivation product) suggests exposure to a xenobiotic that is known to induce IDO1-mediated tryptophan degradation along the kynurenine route, redirecting tryptophan flux away from serotonin/melatonin synthesis toward NAD+ precursor production. N-Formyl-L-glutamic acid and deoxyribose 1-phosphate appear as secondary hits in folate metabolism and the pentose phosphate pathway, respectively.
